Commentary.Commentary: Back with the game. Shafali Verma and Smriti Mandhana to open for India. Lea Tahuhu to bowl first.
...THE CHASE..

India will be disappointed with how they have fielded. If we remeber clearly, they dropped as many as 5 catches today in key situations apart from Radha Yadav who took two insane catches today. Had they took the chances, they would have kept New Zealand Women around 200 but that was not the case. The seamers went for plenty initially and Harmanpreet Kaur jumped towards her spinners quickly to grab hold of the position. Deepti Sharma bowled well throughout and was the most economial of all. However, Radha Yadav ended with four wickets and was the pick of the lot. India as mentioned earlier could have pulled the game back had they taken their chances or by bowling tightly in the final 10 overs. Now the damage is done! New Zealand Women have got more than the average first innings score here. India have to bat really well. New Zealand Women will fancy they can level the series with a healthy score on the board. Stay tuned.

A competitive score by the Kiwis and they will be really happy with how they have performed. The key was how they started and ended in the innings. First, the openers laid the foundation as they hit the seamers for plenty of runs. Both added more than 50 in the first 10 overs with Bates scoring a fine fifty but Georgia Plimmer fell 9 short of her fifty. New Zealand Women lost 3 wickets in the space of 10 overs but Sophie Devine and Maddy Green joined hands to build a partnership of run a ball 82. Green too fell in her 40s but Devine played a handy innings to get New Zealand Women to a powerful position.

FOUR! How important is this shot? A length ball on off, Kerr smashes it down to long on. Radha Yadav misjudges the flight of the ball and over runs, it goes over her head and into the fence. New Zealand Women end with 259/9.

TOSS - New Zealand Women have won the toss and will BAT.

India Women will hope their star batters can put their hands up. The likes of Smriti Mandhana and Jemimah Rodrigues have enough experience now to take matters into their hands, the duo got off to a start in the first match but couldn't convert into a big score. However, the debutant stepped up for them. Tejal Hasabnis and Saima Thakor were brilliant on their international debut. New Zealand Women on the other hand, bowled well but the batting compartment failed to chase it down on a good track. Let's see if New Zealand Women can put on a good performance today. Stay tuned.

The Women's are back in action once again as we welcome you all to the second ODI between India Women and New Zealand Women. The defending T20I champions New Zealand Women suffered a heavy blow by losing the first game while India Women despite tweaking the team XI got things right to take advantage in the series. Can India Women seal the series or New Zealand Women will level it up? Let's find out.
...MATCH DAY...

It is now time for the 2nd ODI between India Women and New Zealand Women to be played at the Narendra Modi Stadium in Ahmedabad. The Women's T20 World Cup might be over but the champions, the White Ferns are back in action straightaway with a three-match ODI series against India Women in India and it seems the Kiwis are having some post-championship blues as they lost the first ODI pretty comprehensively. Both sides are missing a few key names but both teams have enough star power to catch the attention of the fans and a few of them didn't disappoint. Fresh off her Player of the Tournament accolade in the recently concluded Women's T20 World Cup, Melie Kerr picked up four wickets in the first innings and was surprisingly sent to bat way down the order as she remained unbeaten on 25 with her team getting bundled out for 168 runs while chasing a target of 228. Neither side quite showed consistency with the bat but the hosts had more individuals score in the 30s and the 40s which got them to a respectable total. A couple of inexperienced individuals also stood up for India as Tejal Hasabnis made 42 with the bat and Saima Thakor was very impressive with the ball, picking up a couple of wickets as well. As for New Zealand Women, Melie's sister, Jess Kerr was also impressive with the ball picking up 3 wickets that included the scalps of Smriti Mandhana and Deepti Sharma. Speaking of Deepti Sharma, she yet again showed why she is India's top all-rounder as her exploits with both bat and ball were invaluable in India Women taking the lead in the series. Both teams will be looking to tighten the screws up top with the bat as the likes of Smriti Mandhana, Suzie Bates and Sophie Devine all failed but the middle order for both sides presents a much more positive face. The real battle though will be between the Indian spinners and the Kiwi batters as Sharma and Radha Yadav outclassed the visitors last time around. Can the White Ferns channel that winning spirit and level the series? Or will Mandhana and her troops seal a series win? Only time will tell.
